rationale.usefulness: Typed Choice/Score/Noul primitives and distributions offer actionable routing and ranking integration (ts-intro, ts-confidence); the report proposes a testable teacher-facing pilot rather than asserting deployed gains.
rationale.impact: Separating semantic judgments from application policy could meaningfully improve a class of builder workflows (ts-intro, ts-114), but no independent evaluation establishes broad AI-development transformation.
rationale.novelty: The explicit primitive family and code-composed decision model show meaningful product differentiation (ts-intro); images and Box expand it but remain experimental rather than a demonstrated new general capability.
rationale.maturity: Versioned API and detailed context/confidence documentation establish usability, while 1.14 preview mapping, experimental capabilities, language unevenness and absent execution tests impose material limits (ts-models, ts-114).
rationale.openness: Published interface and exact confidence formulas improve inspectability; reviewed sources establish a hosted service without open weights, local execution or reproducible training (ts-confidence, ts-models).

concerns: Non-blocking: official vendor evidence only; workload calibration, billing and educational outcomes remain untested.
Chrome spot-check on 2026-10-18 confirmed Choice/Score confidence formula distinctions, Noul absence of confidence, $0.042/M input pricing, latest/preview mappings and context limits.
